inputs.original_text: Folks, we are looking at a glaring warning sign of how unregulated global capitalism and predatory external forces are poised to exploit a developing nation in transition. Let's look at the harsh structural reality here: decades of systemic inequality and institutional impoverishment have left ordinary Cuban residents owning nothing and struggling in poverty. They are structurally barred from taking over the few functioning businesses on the island. And who is waiting in the wings to capitalize on this manufactured vulnerability? A wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors are ready to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices. This is the playbook of disaster capitalism—stripping the assets of working people and handing community wealth over to the privileged few, completely bypassing any collective ownership or labor rights for the people who actually built and sustained that society.

And who is waiting in the wings to capitalize on this manufactured vulnerability? A wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors are ready to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices. This is the exact playbook of disaster capitalism—stripping the assets of working people and handing community wealth over to the privileged few, completely bypassing any collective ownership or labor rights for the people who actually built and sustained that society.

rationales.entity_drift: The principal actors are unchanged, though the modified version omits the description of Cuba as a developing nation in transition.
rationales.relation_drift: The original attributes an intention to exploit the nation to external forces; the modified text instead says those forces drive disaster capitalism. The prospective purchases and residents' exclusion remain the same.
rationales.contradiction_drift: The modified text introduces no internal contradiction.
